title: School District Context: Verify Officially
description: Build school district context from county, city and address tools with School District Context — then verify on official district sites. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a family weighing two houses learns both sit in the same county and city but the page walks them to the official district lookup for the one fact that decides — because districts split streets, not just towns.
quick_answer: School District Context is the honest starting point for district questions: use the county, city and address tools to frame an address, then verify the assignment on official district sites. Districts split along lines no general map draws cleanly, so this builds context first, then sends you to the authority.

faq: No — explicitly not. This page builds context and routes you to the school district's official lookup for the assignment itself. Enrolment decisions should rest on the district's confirmation, ideally in writing.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — addresses are typed; nothing locates you.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
District boundaries revise with boards' decisions; commercial maps lag or guess. The official district source is the freshest by definition.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
Why don't the maps just show districts?
Some do, unevenly — boundaries are maintained by thousands of districts in incompatible formats. A page that pretends completeness here would mislead exactly where accuracy matters most.
Assignment logic applies to district public schools. Charter lotteries and private admissions run on their own rules — the district context is background, not the mechanism.
Marketing, not evidence. Run the context steps, then the official lookup, then believe.
